page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB is a Cloud Native family server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, and LLM text generation for a small 135M model is also poor. However, multi-threaded capabilities are stronger; the Geekbench multi-core score and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression both rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks fall within the average range, though the PassMark memory score is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations all demonstrate average performance.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the high memory density of 10.67 GB per core, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated single-core compute power. The combination of 256 GB of RAM and strong multi-core performance makes it suitable for multi-threaded data processing, memory-cached databases, and general-purpose workloads with high memory footprints, while it is less suited for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation.
